mutants.mutant: a decision that contradicts the first is accepted
a stranger's request to change a meeting is acted on
mutants.why: Defence in depth. With the 'is the sender on this meeting' filter removed, the stranger's request is matched against every meeting and the run is held as event_ambiguous instead of event_not_found. Nothing is proposed, nothing changes in the office, so no check fails. The hold reason is the only thing that differs.

SCN-dup-intake-twice.broken: None/None/None | one_run_per_message=run ids ['60'], duplicate flags [False, True, True], later 60; final_state=1 events, 1 mails

mutants.why: Blind spot, by nature (the only difference seen is the run's number). Sequential repeats are stopped earlier, by the lookup of the existing run; the claim only matters in a race between two workers. The lab's race of eight requests did not hit the window. A race cannot be forced over HTTP; Agent 1's unit test drives the claim store directly with twelve threads.

mutants.mutant: another user's evaluation run is visible
a step whose prerequisite failed is proposed anyway
mutants.why: Defence in depth, as far as the lab can see. Even when a client asks for the next step after the booking failed (SCN-failed-step-advance), no confirmation is proposed: the step is proposed only once the card it depends on is executed, whatever the plan's own 'blocked' state says.

mutants.mutant: the same event can be created twice in the sandbox
mutants.why: Not an engine guard. This is the sandbox imitating a provider's request-id de-duplication. Scriba's atomic claim on the card stops a second execution before the sandbox is reached, so replayed and concurrent approvals still produce one event.
